strongest_angle: The James Webb Space Telescope and Gemini North telescope discovered the oldest compact quasar pair, designated J1602+4228AB, existing just 900 million years after the Big Bang.

key_facts.fact: The Gemini North telescope on Maunakea and the James Webb Space Telescope observed a pair of rapidly feeding supermassive black holes just 900 million years after the Big Bang.
An international team of astrophysicists led by Silvia Onorato of NSF NOIRLab discovered the compact quasar pair object J1602+4228AB.
JWST’s Aether survey spotted a companion to quasar J1602+4228A during visual inspection of its data set, and Gemini North ground observations separated the two quasars.
